story.title: Story 1: Session Lifecycle and Thread Resolution

result.reviewScopeSummary: Follow-up verification focused on prior SV-001 and SV-002 plus directly touched lifecycle surfaces. The configured gates pass, and the module-scope reload memory was removed, but both prior blockers now depend on explicit spec deviations that require human ruling before the story can pass.

priorFindingStatuses.rationale: The module-scope thread id was removed, but reload for no-flag and --resume now reattaches to the cwd's most-recent registry row rather than reconstructing from the resolved thread id required by AC-1.5. The implementor artifact and code both identify this as an Epic-1 convenience with a known concurrent same-cwd limitation and defer precise lineage to Feature 2+.

The production path now shows the cwd-scoped title/created/id list through ctx.ui.notify, but it still auto-selects the most recent thread. AC-1.7 requires resolving the operator's selection; the implementor records this as a spec deviation because PI v0.79.2 exposes no interactive selection surface.

openFindings.title: Reload reconstruction still does not use the resolved thread id for no-flag and --resume reloads
openFindings.evidence: AC-1.5 requires reload reconstruction from durable state, specifically the resolved thread id (story lines 51-53). The revised resolveReloadThread handles --session by id, but for no-flag and --resume it lists threads by cwd and chooses listed.value.at(-1) at packages/pi-lhc/src/lifecycle/thread-resolution.ts:118-147. The implementor artifact records that a concurrent same-cwd session could be selected instead and defers precise reload lineage to Feature 2+. The test at packages/pi-lhc/test/lifecycle/thread-resolution.test.ts:335-370 proves only the single-thread-in-cwd case, not reconstruction from the prior resolved thread id.

openFindings.title: Production --resume still does not resolve an operator selection
openFindings.evidence: AC-1.7 requires --resume/-r to list cwd-scoped threads with title and creation time and resolve the operator's selection (story lines 59-61; tech design lines 231 and 251-253). The revised defaultSelectThread shows the list via ctx.ui.notify but then returns mostRecent.threadId at packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts:157-176. The production test asserts notification plus most-recent behavior at packages/pi-lhc/test/lifecycle/thread-resolution.test.ts:255-290. The implementor artifact records this as a spec deviation because the available PI UI surface has notify but no interactive input.

verified: AC-1.1 / TC-1.1: no-flag session_start creates one cwd/title registry thread and one background LHC instance; lifecycle tests and pi-lhc verify pass.
AC-1.2 / TC-1.2: existing --session launch attaches to the existing thread and creates no second thread.
AC-1.3 / TC-1.3 plain-data holder: connector snapshot remains structuredClone-able across fresh ctx objects.
AC-1.4 / TC-1.4: shutdown dispose flush preserves pre-shutdown intake events across re-resolve.
AC-1.6 / TC-1.6: launch modes and bad/ambiguous id behavior remain covered.
A-8 registry support remains covered by lhc threads-a8 focused test.
unverified: AC-1.5 / TC-1.5 for no-flag and --resume reload reconstruction from the resolved thread id; current implementation uses cwd-most-recent registry selection.
AC-1.7 / TC-1.7 production operator selection; current implementation presents choices but auto-selects most recent.

gatesRun.command: pnpm --filter pi-lhc exec vitest run test/lifecycle/instance.test.ts test/lifecycle/thread-resolution.test.ts
pnpm --filter lhc exec vitest run test/threads-a8.test.ts

productionPathFindings: Reload production path for no-flag/--resume uses cwd-most-recent registry selection, not the prior resolved thread id.
Production --resume presents choices through notify but auto-selects most recent; there is no real operator selection in the production path.
openQuestions: Does Lee accept cwd-most-recent registry reattach as satisfying AC-1.5 for Story 1 despite the known concurrent same-cwd limitation?
Does Lee accept notify-list plus most-recent default as satisfying AC-1.7 until PI exposes an interactive selection surface?
additionalObservations: The story and epic gates pass: pi-lhc verify and verify-all both passed with 33 tests.
The prior module-scope reload memory implementation is gone; the remaining SV-001 issue is the replacement behavior, not retained module state.
The fail-closed observeOnlyProvider remains unchanged from the prior review and was not part of the follow-up fix surface.
